label: Quotes
value: > Anne Shirley,” reluctantly faltered forth the owner of that name, “but, oh, please do call me Cordelia. It can’t matter much to you what you call me if I’m only going to be here a little while, can it? And Anne is such an unromantic name.

label: Quotes
value: > I shall never forgive Gilbert Blythe,” said Anne firmly. “And Mr. Phillips spelled my name without an e, too. The iron has entered into my soul, Diana.

label: Quotes
value: > I shall take more interest than ever in my studies now,” said Anne blissfully, “because I have a purpose in life. Mr. Allan says everybody should have a purpose in life and pursue it faithfully. Only he says we must first make sure that it is a worthy purpose. I would call it a worthy purpose to want to be a teacher like Miss Stacy, wouldn’t you, Marilla? I think it’s a very noble profession.

label: Quotes
value: > You both have the advantage of me,” sighed Anne. “You’re going to teach children who don’t know you, but I have to teach my own old schoolmates, and Mrs. Lynde says she’s afraid they won’t respect me as they would a stranger unless I’m very cross from the first. But I don’t believe a teacher should be cross. Oh, it seems to me such a responsibility!

label: Quotes
value: > Phil, you’re incorrigible. Well, I love you so much that I can’t make nice, light, congratulatory little speeches. But I’m heart-glad of your happiness.

value: Anne is an imaginative girl.
unit: Anne is an imaginative, enthusiastic, and talkative girl who throws herself into her studies and endeavors heart and soul. She possesses a vivid imagination that allows her to dream up elaborate scenarios, though it occasionally gets her into trouble or causes her to borrow unnecessary care. Intense in both her affections and her rivalries, she can hold grudges with strong tenacity, yet she is generous, courageous, and quick to take responsibility and confess when she realizes her mistakes.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley came to Green Gables
unit: Anne Shirley came to Green Gables as an eleven-year-old orphan and was taken in by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert. She quickly formed a deep bond with her bosom friend Diana Barry and attended school in Avonlea under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy. Driven by a intense academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe, she excelled in her studies, joined the Queen's class, and earned her teacher's license at Queen's Academy. Although awarded the Avery scholarship, she gave up college to stay at home with Marilla after Matthew's death and taught at Avonlea school. During her time as a teacher, she served as secretary of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and gained a neighborly friend in Mr. Harrison. She later attended Redmond College in Kingsport, rooming at Patty's Place with friends including Priscilla Grant and Philippa Gordon, before returning to teach as a country schoolma'am at Valley Road.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye is an orphan.
unit: Anthony Pye, an orphan, was taken in by his aunt, Mrs. George Pye, and began attending Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. From the beginning, he displayed a hostile attitude toward Anne, remarking that she was not any good just like all girl teachers. On one occasion, he poured water from his slate bottle down Aurelia Clay's neck and remained indifferent to Anne's gentle lecture on being a gentleman. Although he rarely openly disobeyed Anne, he obeyed with a scornful air that undermined her authority. Later, after putting a live mouse in Anne's desk drawer, he was whipped by Anne using a pointer, which reduced him to tears and caused Anne to regret losing any remaining chance of winning his affection.

label: Quotes
value: > It’s a very old-fashioned way. But I am old-fashioned. My clothes are, and it stands to reason my opinions are, too. I don’t say they’re any the better of that, mind you. In fact, I daresay they’re a good deal the worse. But they’ve worn nice and easy. New shoes are smarter than old ones, but the old ones are more comfortable. I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions. I mean to take it real easy here. I know you expect me to look after you and keep you proper, but I’m not going to do it. You’re old enough to know how to behave if you’re ever going to be. So, as far as I am concerned, you can all go to destruction in your own way.

label: Quotes
value: > There’s magic in the words ‘silk’ and ‘lace,’ isn’t there? The very sound of them makes me feel like skipping off to a dance. And yellow silk. It makes one think of a dress of sunshine. I always wanted a yellow silk dress, but first my mother and then my husband wouldn’t hear of it. The very first thing I’m going to do when I get to heaven is to get a yellow silk dress.

label: Quotes
value: > If you are going to marry a minister, you will have to give up such expressions as ‘dig in.’

label: Quotes
value: > It isn’t in good taste to make fun of your beaux; but, I always did it myself.

label: History
value: Elizabeth married
unit: Left alone in a large house after her daughter Elizabeth married and went to the foreign mission field in India, Aunt Jamesina accepted an invitation to move to Kingsport to keep house at Patty's Place for college students Anne, Priscilla, Phil, and Stella. During cold winter nights, she allowed the cats—Rusty, Joseph, and the Sarah-cat—to sleep indoors, taking comfort in the Sarah-cat's purring to soothe her fears about snakes in India. After the students graduated, she remained at Patty's Place to care for the cats, preferring it over opening her own home or visiting. Later, despite her terror of snakes, she traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field.

value: Billy drove Anne Shirley and Jane Andrews in a double-seated buggy.

value: Captain Jim is a tall sailor.

His deep-set blue eyes are remarkably bright, sometimes twinkling or dreaming, and often gazing seaward with a wistful quest.

label: Personality
value: Captain Jim is a high-souled man.
unit: Captain Jim is a high-souled, simple-minded, and cheerful man possessing eternal youth in his heart and eyes. A passionate worshipper of beauty, he finds subtle joy in every lovely sight or sound. He is placid and virtually impossible to anger, preferring to defend others against unproven accusations. Marked by a chronic habit of enjoying life and a deep mixture of kindness and wisdom, he embraces both joyous and disagreeable things with humor and philosophical grace.

label: History
value: Captain Jim spent his childhood in Four Winds.
unit: Captain Jim spent his childhood in Four Winds, befriending local schoolmaster John Selwyn at age sixteen. Coming from a line of seafarers, he ran off to sea as a boy and spent the next six decades traveling all over the world. Over fifty years ago, he lost his sweetheart Margaret when her dory drifted out to sea during a sudden storm. After searching the shoreline in vain for months, he carried her memory with him through all his voyages. Five years before meeting Anne Blythe, he gave up seafaring and became the keeper of the Four Winds Point lighthouse. During his travels, he discovered an amnesiac, injured Dick Moore in Cuba and brought him home to Leslie Moore. He rescued a abandoned cat, naming him the First Mate, and regularly visited Anne and Gilbert Blythe, forming a close bond with them as kindred spirits. Together with author Owen Ford, he collaborated to publish his life's experiences in a book titled The Life-Book of Captain Jim. After seeing the publication of his life-book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully.

label: Quotes
value: > Miss Lavendar isn’t well, Miss Shirley, ma’am. I’m sure she isn’t, though she never complains.

label: Quotes
value: > Please, Miss Shirley, ma’am, it’s plain to be seen you and Miss Lavendar have got a secret and I think, begging your pardon if I’m too forward, Miss Shirley, ma’am, that it’s real mean not to tell me when we’ve all been such chums.

label: Quotes
value: > I hope that he’ll marry Miss Lavendar. Some women’s intended from the start to be old maids, and I’m afraid I’m one of them, Miss Shirley, ma’am, because I’ve awful little patience with the men.

label: Quotes
value: > Goodness, no, Miss Shirley, ma’am. I wouldn’t know who he meant if he did. Of course, when we got married he had to say, 'I take thee, Leonora,’ and I declare to you, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’ve had the most dreadful feeling ever since that it wasn’t me he was talking to and I haven’t been rightly married at all.

label: Quotes
value: > Tom is only a bricklayer, but he’s real good-tempered. When I said to him, says I, 'Tom, can I go to Miss Shirley’s wedding? I mean to go anyhow, but I’d like to have your consent,’ he just says, 'Suit yourself, Charlotta, and you’ll suit me.’ That’s a real pleasant kind of husband to have, Miss Shirley, ma’am.

value: Charlotta is warm-hearted.

Although somewhat prone to clumsiness and self-conscious about her lack of patience with men, she holds affection and care for those she serves.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman is nicknamed Charlotta the Fourth by Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Leonora Bowman, nicknamed Charlotta the Fourth by Miss Lavendar Lewis, came to live at Echo Lodge at age fourteen to work as Miss Lavendar's handmaiden following her three elder sisters. She developed a deep adoration for her mistress and became fond of Anne Shirley and Diana Barry during their frequent visits to the lodge. Worried about Miss Lavendar's health and lonely future, she actively supported Anne's efforts to help Miss Lavendar and rejoiced when Miss Lavendar married Mr. Stephen Irving. Following the wedding, she moved with the Irvings to Boston, though she initially experienced severe homesickness. She matured into a young lady, discarded her oversized blue hair bows, and eventually married a good-tempered bricklayer named Tom. Later, she returned to attend Anne's wedding, enthusiastically throwing rice and old shoes to wish the bride good luck.

label: History
value: Cornelia grew up as an only child for eight years.
unit: Miss Cornelia grew up as an only child for eight years before her younger brother was born. In her youth, she had her pick of suitors but remained unmarried for many years, earning a reputation in Four Winds for her sharp tongue and kind nature. She formed a close friendship with Leslie Moore, standing by her as her best friend and helper through hardship. Upon meeting Anne Blythe, Cornelia recognized a kindred spirit and quickly became a frequent visitor at the Blythe house, engaging in lively verbal sparring matches with her old friend Captain Jim. She later arranged for Owen Ford to board with Leslie and loyally defended Leslie against local gossip. Eventually, Cornelia agreed to marry Marshall Elliott, satisfied at least by the fact that he was a fellow Presbyterian.

label: History
value: Davy Keith was orphaned.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned when their sick mother, Mary, passed away. Being third cousins to Marilla Cuthbert, the twins were taken in at Green Gables. Davy's lack of early training and upbringing initially resulted in great distraction and constant mischief, such as shutting Dora up, telling lies, falling into lemon pies, and hanging over the well to look for the dark. Under Anne Shirley's affectionate guidance and Marilla's firm discipline, Davy gradually reformed. He started attending Avonlea school, where he shared a desk with Milty Boulter and developed a keen rivalry over their height. As he grew older, Davy developed a strong interest in farming and expressed a desire to try running the Green Gables farm.

label: History
value: Dora's father died.
unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy were orphaned at a young age after their father died and their sick mother passed away. He later attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne, completing the Second Year work in a single year to earn a First Class teacher's license. He served as the president of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society during this period and actively planned local enhancements. Moving on to Redmond College, Gilbert excelled as a student, leading the Freshmen in the Arts Rush, serving as class president, and playing as captain of the Freshman football team. He eventually graduated with High Honors in Classics, winning the prestigious Cooper Prize. Following a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, he reconciled with Anne, leading to their eventual marriage in the orchard at Green Gables. Settling in Four Winds, Gilbert succeeded his great-uncle as the local country doctor and built a home with Anne, becoming a father to their son, Little Jem.

label: History
value: Mr. J. A. Harrison originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick.
unit: Mr. J. A. Harrison originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick. After his sister died, he married Emily Scott to fulfill a deathbed promise, but the two separated over household friction and her hatred of his parrot, Ginger. Harrison subsequently moved to Prince Edward Island and purchased Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea. Initially viewed as an eccentric bickering crank by the community, he hired John Henry Carter and lived a bachelor's life. He eventually formed a warm friendship with his young neighbor, Anne Shirley. Later, his wife Emily arrived in Avonlea and reconciled with him following Ginger's death. Following his reunion with Emily, Harrison became a regular churchgoer who subscribed to the minister's salary, growing increasingly sociable and well-regarded in the community.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Growing up in Avonlea as the daughter of Harmon Andrews, Jane attended the local school, participated in the childhood Story Club, and joined in games and dares with her playmates. She attended Queen's Academy in the teacher's course, excelling in domestic science. Upon obtaining her license, she began her career teaching school in Newbridge while serving as committee chairman in the Avonlea Voluntary Improvement Society. She later spent time teaching on the western prairies. Before leaving for the West, she acted as a spokesperson on behalf of her brother Billy's romantic interest in Anne Shirley. She eventually returned home to marry Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, and spent her wedding tour travelling to Europe. Despite her wealth, she remained a kind, unaffected friend to her old Avonlea companions.

value: Josie attended Avonlea school.
unit: Josie attended Avonlea school, where she was the last of the long-standing Pye family to be enrolled. label: History
value: Lavendar lived a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge.
unit: Lavendar lived a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge, where she employed a young handmaiden whom she called Charlotta the Fourth. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited her, quickly forming a close bond over tea and shared imagination. After meeting Stephen Irving's son Paul, Lavendar formed a fond friendship with him and later reconnected with Stephen himself. The long-separated couple reconciled and were married in a late August ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor. Following their wedding, Lavendar relocated with Stephen, Paul, and Charlotta the Fourth, later settling into their new home where she remained perfectly happy.

value: > I was sixteen. I am twenty-eight now. Well, I must go back.

value: > I ENVY Anne, and I’d envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I’d gladly give my life for THAT!

value: > There is no cage. But—it doesn’t seem as if there were anything else, Anne. You—you remember what I told you of my folly that night on the sand-bar? label: History
value: Leslie West is the daughter of Frank West
unit: Leslie West grew up as the daughter of Frank and Rose West, surviving the traumatic childhood loss of her brother Kenneth and later finding her father after his suicide. She studied at Queen's Academy using an inheritance from her grandmother and became a schoolteacher at the Glen school. At sixteen, she was coerced into marrying Dick Moore to save her mother's farm from foreclosure, and she lost her mother to pneumonia a year later. After her husband was believed to have returned mentally incapacitated from a sea voyage, she faithfully nursed him for years in poverty. Following Gilbert Blythe's suggestion, she agreed to take him to Montreal for an operation, where it was discovered that the man was actually Dick's lookalike cousin, George Moore, freeing her from her long burden. She later fell in love with Owen Ford, accepting his proposal of marriage, and made plans to marry him at Christmas.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables her whole life with her brother Matthew. Deciding to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, they were mistakenly sent Anne Shirley, whom Marilla agreed to keep and raise. Despite her strict nature, Marilla grew deeply attached to Anne as she mentored her into womanhood. Following Matthew's death and a period of failing eyesight, she took in the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. Over the years, her lifelong friendship with Rachel Lynde deepened, leading Rachel to move in with her at Green Gables. Marilla took great pride and quiet joy in Anne's academic successes and eventual marriage to Gilbert Blythe, the son of her former youth courtier John Blythe. In her later years, she ventured beyond Avonlea for the first time to visit Anne and Gilbert in Four Winds.

Despite her strict nature, Marilla grew deeply attached to Anne as she mentored her into womanhood. Following Matthew's death and a period of failing eyesight, she took in the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. Over the years, her lifelong friendship with Rachel Lynde deepened, leading Rachel to move in with her at Green Gables. Marilla took great pride and quiet joy in Anne's academic successes and eventual marriage to Gilbert Blythe, the son of her former youth courtier John Blythe. In her later years, she ventured beyond Avonlea for the first time to visit Anne and Gilbert in Four Winds.

label: History
value: Fifteen years before the Liberals came into power, Marshall Elliott fought tooth and nail for his political party during a bitter general election.
unit: Fifteen years before the Liberals came into power, Marshall Elliott fought tooth and nail for his political party during a bitter general election and vowed at a public meeting not to cut his hair or shave his beard until the Grits gained power. True to his word, he grew out his hair and beard for fifteen years, looking like an eccentric to strangers. During this time, he spent leisure hours cod-fishing with Captain Jim and visiting friends at the lighthouse, where he entertained others by telling stories, singing old Scotch ballads, and dancing with Leslie Moore. When the Liberals finally won the election, Marshall went to the barber before sunrise to be shaved and have his hair cut. Shortly after, he became engaged to Miss Cornelia Bryant.

Although he later travelled across the country to Vancouver, he returned to Four Winds in August to court Leslie, ultimately reaching an understanding with her in the garden.

During her college years, she resides at Patty's Place alongside Anne, Priscilla, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina. While torn between her two suitors from home, Alec and Alonzo, Phil meets Jonas Blake while spending a summer at Prospect Point and falls deeply in love with him. Despite her mother's initial objections to his modest career as a minister, Phil stands firm and wins her family's approval. After winning a mathematical scholarship, she marries Jonas in Bolingbroke shortly after graduation, changing her name to Phil Blake. She later writes a letter to Gilbert Blythe explaining that Anne's engagement to Roy Gardner is over, prompting Gilbert to resume his courtship of Anne. Phil and Jonas later welcome children and attend Anne's wedding at Green Gables.

value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea. During his tenure, he regularly courted his student Prissy Andrews under the guise of helping her with her lessons, showing her special attention in and out of class. He enforced strict discipline inconsistently, such as calling out Anne Shirley for spelling mistakes, making her stand on the platform, and punishing students who returned late from recess. He once whipped Sam Boulter for being impudent, which caused Sam's father to confront him at school. He later gave a tearful farewell speech to his pupils at the end of his final term before leaving Avonlea.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy, where she formed a close circle of friends with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. She later taught school in Carmody before taking her own home school. While on the Island, she presented a paper on cemeteries to the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and brought her aunt, the famous writer Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan, to visit Anne at Green Gables. Priscilla went on to attend Redmond College in Kingsport, living as housemates with Anne Shirley, Philippa Gordon, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina at Patty's Place. In her senior year at Redmond, she focused her studies on classics. Following college, she married a handsome foreign missionary and relocated to Japan.

Priscilla went on to attend Redmond College in Kingsport, living as housemates with Anne Shirley, Philippa Gordon, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina at Patty's Place. In her senior year at Redmond, she focused her studies on classics. Following college, she married a handsome foreign missionary and relocated to Japan.

label: Personality
value: Rachel Lynde is a capable woman.
unit: Rachel Lynde is a capable, practical, and hardworking woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. Highly opinionated, critical, and curious, she loves to keep a sharp eye on community business and dearly loves to be asked for advice. Despite being a meddlesome gossip who can be compulsively corrective and strict, she is fundamentally a good, kind-hearted Christian woman. She is a passionate, red-hot politician, yet remains a tender and devoted nurse to her sick husband.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the main road in Avonlea
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the main road in Avonlea, where she kept a sharp eye on all community happenings while keeping house and running local societies. When Marilla Cuthbert adopted Anne Shirley, Rachel criticized the child's looks, prompting an angry outburst from Anne; Rachel later acknowledged her error as Anne matured. When her husband Thomas fell gravely ill, Rachel nursed him untiringly until his death. Facing financial difficulties after his passing due to an earlier farm mortgage, she accepted Marilla's invitation to move to Green Gables to live together, freeing Anne to attend college. Later, she traveled from Avonlea to Four Winds to spend Christmas with Anne and Gilbert.

label: History
value: Jonas Blake was a theological student
unit: Jonas Blake was a theological student from St. Columbia who previously graduated from Redmond College. While studying, he took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church for a summer, where he met Philippa Gordon and quickly became close friends with her. Although he resisted entering the ministry for a long time, he eventually accepted it as his divine calling. He frequently visited Patty's Place while traveling from St. Columbia and became a general favorite there. After proposing to Philippa, he visited her home at Mount Holly and won over her parents despite initial reservations from her mother. Upon graduating from St. Columbia, he took charge of a small mission church on Patterson Street in the slums and married Philippa Gordon. Later, Jonas attended the wedding of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe, where he offered a prayer praised by Mrs. Rachel Lynde, before residing in Kingsport with his wife.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner interrupted his studies at Redmond College.
unit: Roy Gardner interrupted his studies at Redmond College to accompany his sick mother abroad for two years, taking the disappointment graciously. Upon returning to college, he began courting Anne Shirley, lavishing her with flowers, sonnets, and romantic compliments. His devotion was widely noticed across Redmond, and most residents of Patty's Place liked him, though the house cat took an immediate dislike to him. He frequently sent exquisite letters and took Anne out socially throughout her college years. Eventually, he introduced Anne to his mother and sisters, among whom Dorothy was his favorite. He proposed marriage to Anne, but she refused him, leaving him looking pale and foolish, as he had felt confident of her acceptance.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school alongside Anne Shirley and her friends. As a student, she climbed a willow tree on a dare, took part in school entertainments, and passed the Entrance examinations to Queen's Academy. After graduating from Queen's with her teaching license, she taught at a school up west before taking over the Carmody school. Later, she was rumored to be engaged to a Spencervale schoolmaster, whom she turned down. She contracted galloping consumption, forcing her to stop teaching during the winter, though she still hoped to teach at White Sands. During her illness, she reconciled an old school quarrel with Em White and spent a quiet final evening conversing with Anne Shirley. She died peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter.

After graduating from Queen's with her teaching license, she taught at a school up west before taking over the Carmody school. Later, she was rumored to be engaged to a Spencervale schoolmaster, whom she turned down. She contracted galloping consumption, forcing her to stop teaching during the winter, though she still hoped to teach at White Sands. During her illness, she reconciled an old school quarrel with Em White and spent a quiet final evening conversing with Anne Shirley. She died peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the trustees
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the trustees as Avonlea's first female schoolteacher. Upon taking up her post, she introduced fresh teaching methods, including biweekly recitation afternoons, field days in the woods to study nature, and daily physical culture exercises. She formed a dedicated Queen's class to prepare pupils for the Entrance examinations to Queen's Academy. At one point, she was offered a position in the grade school of her home district, but she returned to Avonlea to teach the class through their final year. At the end of June, her tenure as Avonlea's schoolteacher came to a close, leaving her pupils deeply moved as she said her farewells. She advised Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe to take up Second Year work at Queen's Academy to obtain First Class licenses in a single year.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy, where she studied in the Second Year classes and formed a close circle of intimate friends with Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant. After her time at Queen's, she spent time working as a schoolteacher. She later wrote to Anne proposing that they rent Patty's Place together so she could attend Redmond College while her aunt kept house for them. During her college years, she lived at Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, Philippa Gordon, and her Aunt Jamesina, achieving a good all-round academic standing at graduation. After completing her studies, Stella moved to Vancouver, where she resumed teaching school.

label: History
value: Susan Baker was installed as the maid-of-all-work.
unit: Susan Baker was installed as the maid-of-all-work at the little house of Anne and Gilbert Blythe. When Anne took ill, Susan actively looked after her, taking offense when Cornelia Bryant brought food under the belief that her own cooking was superior. Gilbert insisted that Susan be retained for the summer to manage the household and look after Anne. Later, when her sister Matilda broke her leg, Susan temporarily departed her duties at the little house to care for her, despite noting that no one in her family had ever broken a leg before. She eventually returned to continue helping the doctor and his wife.
